newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures dip at close, seen supported.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures dip at close, seen supported.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended slightly easier on Wednesday but dealers said the market looked well supported and was likely to extend its recent gains.
The lead Nikkei 225 June contract ended 15 points easier at 20,535 after hitting a high of 20,745 on volume of 13,250 lots.
"People were buying on small volume in the morning. There's no news in the market so the trading is mainly on technicals," a trader with a Japanese futures house said.
He said the June Nikkei could test the downside but was unlikely to fall below 20,400 before heading upwards to 20,800.

Dealers said the market was unmoved by news a subcommittee of Japan's Ministry of International Trade and Industry was calling for sweeping financial reforms before the revision of foreign exchange laws nest April.

"They are likely to have some problems pushing the reforms forward. There will be resistance from broking houses over the deregulation of commissions," the trader said, adding that the news would not have any immediate impact on the market.
The June MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 348.6 against their opening 349.4 on low volume of 224 lots.
